The Special Deputy Collector, vs Topaz Welfare Association
Retd on 10 January, 2025

entities.text: Special Deputy Collector, vs Topaz Welfare Association
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Author: Abhinand Kumar Shavili
Bench: Abhinand Kumar Shavili
 Hon'Ble Sri Justice Abhinand Kumar Shavili
 And
Hon'Ble Sri Justice Laxmi Narayana Alishetty
 LAAS.No.86 of 2016
Judgment:

(per Hon'ble Sri Justice Laxmi Narayana Alishetty) Heard learned Assistant Government Pleader for Appeals appearing for the appellant-Land Acquisition Officer and Sri N.Vasudeva Reddy,
learned counsel for the respondent- claimant.

2. This Appeal, under Section 54 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, (for brevity 'the Act'), is filed by the Land Acquisition Officer aggrieved by the order and decree dated 05.12.2014 passed in O.P.No.1174 of 2013 on the file of the II Additional Chief Judge, City Civil Courts, Hyderabad, (for brevity, hereinafter referred to as "the Reference Court").

entities.text: II Additional Chief Judge, City Civil Courts, Hyderabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
3. In nut-shell, the facts of the case are that on a requisition made by the Assistant City Planner,
Circle-V, Municipal Corporation of Hyderabad, the property bearing Municipal No.6-3- 883/A/13 admeasuring 456.40 square yards in 'Topaz' building Complex, Amrutha Hills, Hyderabad, which belongs to the respondent-claimant was acquired for the purpose of road widening from Panjagutta to Rajiv Gandhi Statue Main Road, Somajiguda, 2 AKS, J & LNA, J Hyderabad; that Draft notification under Section 4(1) of the Act was published in the Official Gazette on 25.02.2005; that draft declaration under Section 6 of the Act was published in Official Gazette on 25.07.2005; that after following the procedure prescribed under the Act and on conducting enquiry, the Land Acquisition Officer passed an Award, dated 16.03.2006, fixing the market value of the acquired land @ Rs.6,000/- per square yard.
4.

As the respondent/claimant did not furnish the documents showing its ownership over the subject acquired property, the Land Acquisition Officer has referred the matter to the competent Civil Court under Sections 18 and 30 of the Act and the same was numbered as L.A.O.P.No.1174 of 2013 on the file of the Reference Court.
5. Before the Reference Court, on behalf of the respondent/claimant, P.Ws.1 and 2 were examined and Exs.A-1 to A-10 were marked.
On behalf of the appellant-Referring Officer, R.W-1 was examined, but no documents were marked.

The Special Deputy Collector, vs Topaz Welfare Association Retd on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93212465/
1 6.

entities.text: Special Deputy Collector, vs Topaz Welfare Association Retd on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On due appreciation of the oral and documentary evidence available on record, the Reference Court held that the respondent/claimant is the owner of the subject acquired property and hence, it is entitled to compensation for the same.

Further, the 3 AKS, J & LNA, J Reference Court has enhanced the market value of the acquired land from Rs.6,000/- per square yard to Rs.17,600/- per square yard, apart from granting other statutory benefits under the Act to the respondent/claimant.
Aggrieved thereby, the present appeal is filed by the Land Acquisition Officer.

7. Learned Assistant Government Pleader for Appeals appearing for the appellant-Land Acquisition Officer contended that the Reference Court erred in enhancing the market value of the acquired land based on Ex.A-7-Market Value Certificate issued by the Sub-Registrar and as such, he sought to set aside the impugned order.
8.

Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent/claimant contended that taking into account the location of the acquired land being prime area, the Reference Court has rightly enhanced the compensation for the acquired land and therefore, there are no merits in this Appeal and the same is liable to be dismissed.

9. In this Appeal, no ground is raised challenging the impugned order of the Reference Court holding the respondent/claimant as owner of the subject acquired property and therefore, the same is not adjudicated by this Court.
4 AKS, J & LNA, J 10.

The respondent/claimant has got marked as many as ten documents viz., Exs.A-1 to A-10 before the Reference Court in support of its claim for enhancement of market value of the subject acquired land fixed by the Land Acquisition Officer.
Among the said documents, Exs.A-6 to A-8 are mainly relied upon by the respondent/claimant for enhancement of market value of the acquired land.

11. It is relevant to note that Exs.A-7 and A-8 are Market Value Certificates issued by the Sub-Registrar, Sanjeeva Reddy Nagar, Hyderabad, whereunder the market value of the land was shown as Rs.17,600/- per square yard.

However, in the light of the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in a catena of judgments, i.e., in BSNL Vs. Nemichand Damodardas1 and Choda Dharampal Reddy Vs. Revenue Divisional Officer, Nalgonda District2, the said documents cannot form basis for determination of market value of the acquired property.

entities.text: Choda Dharampal Reddy Vs. Revenue Divisional Officer, Nalgonda District2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Reference Court has erroneously considered the Market Value Certificates and enhanced the market value of the acquired land based on the said Certificates, which is unsustainable.

That apart, it is pertinent to note that Ex.A-6 is a sale deed, dated 30.06.2005, whereunder a property with built-up area of 2,000 square feet with undivided share of 46.66 square yards was sold for consideration of Rs.20,50,000/-.

The Special Deputy Collector, vs Topaz Welfare Association Retd on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93212465/
2 13.

entities.text: Special Deputy Collector, vs Topaz Welfare Association Retd on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the instant case, 4(1) notification was published on 25.02.2005, thus, Ex.A-6-sale deed is a post-notification sale deed.

However, it relates to property in the same building known as 'Topaz'
building complex, in which the subject property is acquired.

Further, on behalf of the respondent/claimant before the Reference Court, P.W-2-attestor of Ex.A-6-sale deed was examined,
who deposed to the contents of the said document.
No rebuttal evidence was adduced by the Land Acquisition Officer before the Reference Court.
Also, it is apt to note that the genuineness of the said document is neither challenged nor disputed by the Land Acquisition Officer before the Reference Court.
Therefore, the genuineness of the said document cannot be doubted.

14. Further, this Court cannot lose sight of the fact that Ex.A-6 is a combined sale deed in respect of a flat with plinth area of 2,000 square feet with undivided share of 46.66 square yards of land,
whereunder the total sale consideration is shown as Rs.20,50,000/-.
6 AKS, J & LNA, J

In Ex.A-6-sale deed, there is no clear or separate mention of market value of the land and the structure i.e., built up area, except mentioning the market value of the flat along with undivided share of land.

In the absence of such break-up of market value of the flat i.e., built-up area and the undivided share of land, the stand of the respondent/claimant that the market value of the land covered under Ex.A-6-sale deed is Rs.20,000/- per square yard and as such, based on it,
they are seeking enhancement of the market value of the acquired land, cannot be accepted in toto.
15. Admittedly, the property covered under Ex.A-6-sale deed is situated in the third floor of the same building known as 'Topaz' building complex, in which the acquired property is situated and that the acquired property is located in prime area of Hyderabad city and is a prominent commercial area.

Hence, in the backdrop of the aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case, this Court is of the opinion that though Ex.A-6 is a post-notification sale deed, the same cannot be brushed aside altogether completely from consideration as the genuineness of the same is proved by the respondent/claimant beyond any doubt.

The respondent/claimant adduced evidence to establish that the acquired property is capable 7 AKS, J & LNA, J of fetching higher market value than the amount awarded by the Land Acquisition Officer/Collector.

16. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Special Dy. Collector & Anr. v. Kurra Sambasiva Rao & Ors 3 held as under:-
"The Court enjoined to determine the market value on i) objective assessment of the conditions prevailing in the open market ii) the nature of the user of the land to which the land was put on the date of the notification, the situation of the land iii)income derived therefrom and all other relevant attending circumstances.

entities.text: Special Dy. Collector & Anr. v. Kurra Sambasiva Rao & Ors 3
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The market value so determined should be just, adequate and reasonable.

In other words, it must be just equivalent to what the land is capable of fetching in the open market from a willing and prudent The Special Deputy Collector, vs Topaz Welfare Association Retd on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93212465/
3 buyer.
Therefore, the court is required to sit in the arm chair of a bona fide willing and prudent purchaser in the open market and seek an answer to the question whether in the conditions prevailing in the market he would offer the same market value as the court has proposed."

entities.text: Special Deputy Collector, vs Topaz Welfare Association Retd on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 17. In the instant case, if the aforesaid aspects as enumerated by the Hon'ble Supreme Court are considered while determining the market value of the acquired land, this Court is of the opinion that the respondent/claimant is able to establish the nature of use of acquired property i.e., it being used for commercial purpose as on (1997) 6 SCC 41 8 AKS, J & LNA, J the date of 4(1) notification and its location in a prominent commercial area in Hyderabad city.

18. Therefore, in the aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case and for the foregoing reasons, this Court deems that ends of justice would be met, if the market value of the subject acquired land is fixed @ Rs.12,000/- per square yard, which is just and reasonable.

19. Accordingly, this Appeal is disposed of and the impugned order of the Reference Court is modified, decreasing the compensation from Rs.17,600/- per square yard to Rs.12,000/- per square yard for the subject acquired land.
The remaining portion of the impugned order remains unaltered.

It is needless to note that the respondent/claimant is entitled to all the benefits under the Land Acquisition Act, 1854, on the modified market value.
20.
As a sequel, Miscellaneous Petitions pending, if any, shall stand closed.
No costs.
